model_result.answer_summary: COF-3 is the three-arm hydroxy-imine repeat unit; oxidative dehydrogenative ring closure gives the three-benzoxazole COF-4 unit with an H6 loss; COF-5 is the trihydroxy enol-imine unit; and irreversible tautomerization gives the cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione beta-ketoenamine COF-6 unit. Each displayed cell uses the source's central-node convention and has three dashed lines crossing six arene bonds.
assumptions: Problem figure: COF-3 precursors are benzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde and 1,4-diamino-2,5-dihydroxybenzene.
Problem figure: COF-5 precursors are 2,4,6-trihydroxybenzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde and p-phenylenediamine.

Problem statements: COF-3 has an imine IR stretch; COF-4 has no imine stretch, retains another C=N type, and has six fewer H atoms per repeat unit; COF-5 irreversibly isomerizes to COF-6, which has no imine stretch.

Trusted general chemistry: aldehyde-primary-amine condensation forms C(H)=N; an ortho-hydroxy imine oxidatively cyclizes to benzoxazole by loss of O-H and imine-carbon C-H; an ortho-hydroxy imine can tautomerize to a beta-ketoenamine by proton and pi-bond transfer.
Cell convention copied from the problem's COF-1 example: one tritopic node plus the inward halves of three ditopic linkers; each of three dashed lines crosses two linker-ring bonds.
